anya: heads up, I think I found a reproducible correctness glitch in the FP8 mixed-precision matmul path when KV cache padding crosses a 1024 token boundary. small but consistent token drift in outputs after ~1.5k tokens :eyes:
mike: weird — did you run a full deterministic run or just sampling?
anya: deterministic. used our eval harness on the long-context suite, seed fixed, beam=1. diff shows token N+1 changes only when cache length exceeds 1024 and kernel selection switches to fp8-staged kernel.
kevin: any logs or perf traces? could be scale cal mismatch during kernel handoff.
anya: attaching quick snippet of the perf trace:```
[profile] seq_len=1536 model=resX quant_mode=fp8
kernel_choice: matmul_mixed_fp16 -> matmul_fp8_staged at token_index=1024
kv_pad = 32 (align->next_block)
matmul_fp8_staged: scale=0.00391 per-tile
matmul_fp8_ref: scale=0.00488 per-tile
checksum_before=0x7f4a2
checksum_after=0x7f4b8
```
sara: checksum drift small but non-zero — could be quant calibration being re-applied incorrectly after KV padding normalization. we recently changed calibration caching to be per-tile+seqlen, maybe a key generation bug. :thinking_face:
mike: OK repro steps? I can run across GPUs.
anya: `python -m infra.eval_longcontext --model=resX --seq 1536 --quant fp8 --seed 42 --deterministic`
ci-bot: build 2026.03.15-1931: tests/quantization: started
kevin: I ran that locally on A100, reproduced. dump of tile scales shows tile index 3 uses stale calibration for a neighboring tile after pad align. idx3_scale(stale)=0.00586 vs expected 0.00488.
sara: that explains drift. why stale? key used for cache lookup includes seq_len_before_align not after align. fix might be to normalise key by aligned_seq_base.
mike: quick patch idea: when computing quant_key = (model, layer, seq_mod) -> change seq_mod to floor(seq/alignment)*alignment. I'll try in a branch.
anya: also saw perf regression in this path when we force fallback to bf16; batching heuristics flip and latency spikes. might be two separate bugs but both triggered by the same boundary.
kevin: re: tests, add a unit that simulates kv_pad shifting kernel choice: construct kv sizes [1000, 1024, 1536, 2048] and assert identical token logits across them.
sara: +1 on test. also add a trace assert that quant_key used at matmul call equals expected normalised key.
mike: pushed branch `fix/quant-key-align` with tests, CI green locally. link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/abc123
ci-bot: build 2026.03.15-2010: tests/quantization: passed
anya: ran infra eval again on branch — deterministic outputs match across seq boundaries, drift gone. thanks. :tada:
kevin: nice catch. can we add a short perf benchmark for long-context to prevent latency regressions when fallback happens?
sara: I'll add a perf job to the nightly suite, focusing on kernel-handoff latency and batch-size sensitivity.
mike: I'll open a small RFC to document quant_key normalization and the rationale.
anya: owners: mike (patch/RFC), sara (nightly perf), kevin (tests). closing the loop here but leaving thread open if regressions pop back up. :lock_with_ink_pen:
